note: Loop diuretics inhibit the Na-K-2Cl cotransporter and increase calcium loss in urine.
Thiazides inhibit the distal sodium-chloride cotransporter and decrease urine calcium.
Acetazolamide inhibits proximal carbonic anhydrase and causes a normal-anion-gap metabolic acidosis.
Trimethoprim can raise the serum creatinine by blocking secretion, while the glomerular filtration rate stays the same.
An ACE inhibitor dilates the efferent arteriole, so filtration can fall even though kidney perfusion is not worse.
Muddy-brown granular casts mean tubular injury. Hyaline casts alone fit a low-flow prerenal state.
White-cell casts and eosinophiluria after a new drug point to interstitial nephritis, not acute tubular necrosis.
A urine dipstick positive for blood with no red cells on microscopy is myoglobin until proved otherwise.
Vitamin B12 deficiency can damage the dorsal columns. Folate deficiency causes the same anemia without that cord lesion.
Low ferritin means iron deficiency. A high ferritin with low serum iron fits anemia of inflammation.
Primaquine and dapsone can hemolyze red cells that lack glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase. The bite cells appear after the oxidative drug.
Hereditary spherocytosis is a membrane-cytoskeleton defect. Splenectomy stops the hemolysis because the spleen is what removes the spheres.
Hydroxyurea raises fetal hemoglobin, which slows polymerization of sickle hemoglobin.
Immune thrombocytopenia is caused by antibodies against platelet glycoproteins, so platelets are destroyed and production can be impaired.
Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura is a deficiency of ADAMTS13, so huge von Willebrand multimers make platelet thrombi. Platelet transfusion is not the treatment of the count.
Hemophilia A is factor VIII deficiency. Bleeding into a joint with a prolonged PTT and a normal PT fits that factor, not platelets.
Imatinib inhibits the BCR-ABL tyrosine kinase made by the Philadelphia chromosome.
Auer rods are crystalline cytoplasmic inclusions in myeloid blasts and mark acute myeloid leukemia, not acute lymphoblastic leukemia.
Rasburicase breaks down existing uric acid. Allopurinol only decreases formation of new uric acid.
Wilson disease is low ceruloplasmin with copper deposition in liver and basal ganglia. Psychiatric change plus liver disease in a young adult is the clue.
Hereditary hemochromatosis stores iron. Phlebotomy removes it. Deferoxamine is not the first treatment.
Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency can injure both lung and liver, because the protein is not secreted and the lungs lose a shield against elastase.
Pain out of proportion to the exam plus a high lactate is intestinal ischemia until proved otherwise. The next study is vascular imaging, not a laxative.
A serum-ascites albumin gradient of 1.1 g/dL or more means portal hypertension. A low gradient means the fluid is not from portal pressure.
Lactulose treats hepatic encephalopathy by acidifying the colon and trapping ammonia, and by speeding stool loss of nitrogen.
Thiamine is given before glucose in a malnourished patient, because glucose without thiamine can precipitate Wernicke encephalopathy.
Ethosuximide blocks thalamic T-type calcium channels and treats absence seizures. Carbamazepine can worsen absence seizures.
Carbidopa inhibits peripheral dopa decarboxylase so levodopa can reach the brain, and it does not cross into the brain itself in a meaningful way.
Nimodipine after subarachnoid hemorrhage is used to reduce poor outcome from vasospasm. It is not given to clip the aneurysm.
An epidural hematoma is arterial, often from the middle meningeal artery, and classically follows a lucid interval. The CT shape is a lens.
A subdural hematoma comes from bridging veins and spreads in a crescent that can cross suture lines.
Lithium causes nephrogenic diabetes insipidus by resisting antidiuretic hormone in the collecting duct.
Monoamine oxidase inhibitors plus tyramine can cause a hypertensive crisis because dietary amines are not broken down.
SSRIs can cause the syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone, especially in older adults, with low sodium and concentrated urine.
Bupropion lowers the seizure threshold and is avoided in bulimia and in seizure disorders.
Valproate is teratogenic, including neural-tube defects, and is avoided when pregnancy is possible.
Lamotrigine is titrated slowly because a fast start raises the risk of Stevens-Johnson syndrome.
Phenytoin has zero-order kinetics near the therapeutic range, so a small dose increase can cause a large level jump.
Salicylate poisoning causes a respiratory alkalosis and an anion-gap metabolic acidosis together.
Aspirin in a child with a viral illness is linked to Reye syndrome, with liver failure and encephalopathy.
Acetylcysteine restores glutathione so the toxic acetaminophen metabolite can be detoxified.
Bisphosphonates inhibit osteoclasts, so bone resorption falls.
Denosumab is an antibody against RANKL, so osteoclasts are not activated.
Allopurinol blocks formation of new uric acid. It does not dissolve the uric acid already circulating the way rasburicase does.
Warfarin blocks vitamin K epoxide reductase, so factors II, VII, IX, and X and proteins C and S fall.
Warfarin skin necrosis happens when protein C falls before the procoagulant factors, so a transient hypercoagulable state appears.
Heparin binds antithrombin and speeds inactivation of thrombin and factor Xa.
Aspirin irreversibly acetylates cyclooxygenase, so a platelet cannot make thromboxane for the rest of its life.
Spironolactone blocks the aldosterone receptor and the androgen receptor, so potassium rises and breast tissue can enlarge.
Trimethoprim blocks the epithelial sodium channel, like a potassium-sparing diuretic, so potassium can rise.
Nitrofurantoin can hemolyze G6PD-deficient red cells because it is an oxidative drug.
A beta-lactam can cause allergic interstitial nephritis, with fever, rash, and white cells in the urine, days after the drug starts.
Loop diuretics cause metabolic alkalosis by delivering sodium downstream and increasing aldosterone-driven hydrogen and potassium loss.
Thiazides raise serum uric acid and can precipitate gout.
Proton pump inhibitors bind active pumps, so the dose works best before a meal, when pumps are turned on.
The urea breath test detects urease, which Helicobacter uses to split urea into ammonia and carbon dioxide.
HLA-DQ2 or DQ8 is necessary for celiac disease but not sufficient. Most people with the allele do not have the disease.
Benzodiazepines facilitate GABA-A chloride channels. The class does not open glutamate channels.
Succinylcholine can cause fatal hyperkalemia when extrajunctional acetylcholine receptors are upregulated, as after a major burn.
Malignant hyperthermia is a ryanodine-receptor crisis from an anesthetic trigger. Dantrolene closes that calcium release. It is not neuroleptic malignant syndrome.
Allopurinol blocks xanthine oxidase, which also clears the active metabolite of azathioprine, so the azathioprine effect is dangerously increased.
Codeine is a prodrug activated by CYP2D6. Poor metabolizers get little analgesia. Ultra-rapid metabolizers can be toxic.
Simvastatin is cleared by CYP3A4. A strong inhibitor such as clarithromycin can cause statin toxicity and muscle injury.
Carbamazepine induces CYP3A4 and can lower hormonal contraceptive levels, so the contraceptive can fail.
Digoxin toxicity is worsened by low potassium, because potassium and digoxin compete at the sodium-potassium pump.
Naloxone is a competitive mu-opioid antagonist. It reverses opioid respiratory depression and can precipitate withdrawal.
Flumazenil antagonizes benzodiazepines but can precipitate seizures in a person who depends on that drug.
Octreotide constricts splanchnic vessels and lowers portal inflow, which is why it is used in variceal bleeding.
Pleural fluid is an exudate if protein or LDH ratios are high. A transudate is low protein from pressure, as in heart failure.
Statins can injure muscle. A high creatine kinase with pain after a new statin is toxicity, not ordinary soreness to ignore.
Calcium and iron bind levothyroxine in the gut, so the hormone dose should be separated from those supplements.
Primary adrenal failure loses cortisol and aldosterone, so a mineralocorticoid is needed. Secondary adrenal failure keeps aldosterone.
Methimazole blocks thyroid peroxidase, so iodide is not organified into thyroid hormone.
Insulin drives potassium into cells by stimulating the sodium-potassium ATPase. It does not remove potassium from the body.
Intravenous calcium stabilizes the cardiac membrane in hyperkalemia. It does not lower the serum potassium.
Triptans are 5-HT1B/1D agonists. The class constricts cranial vessels and are avoided in coronary disease.
Tardive dyskinesia from long antipsychotic exposure is treated with a VMAT2 inhibitor, not with a higher antipsychotic dose.
A serum-ascites albumin gradient under 1.1 g/dL is not portal hypertension. Peritoneal disease such as carcinomatosis fits a low gradient.
Fluoroquinolones can rupture tendons. A new fluoroquinolone plus tendon pain is a reason to stop the drug.
Fluoroquinolones bind calcium, iron, and other cations, so absorption falls if the doses are taken at the same time.
Linezolid has monoamine-oxidase activity and can cause serotonin syndrome if combined with an SSRI.
Daptomycin is inactivated by pulmonary surfactant, so it is not used for pneumonia.
Acyclovir can crystallize in tubules if the patient is volume depleted. Hydration lowers that risk.
Rifampin induces many CYP enzymes and turns body fluids orange.
Isoniazid increases urinary loss of vitamin B6 and can cause neuropathy. Pyridoxine prevents that.
Ethambutol can cause optic neuropathy, with loss of color vision.
SGLT2 inhibitors can cause ketoacidosis with a glucose that is not very high, because glucose is lost in the urine.
Clozapine can cause agranulocytosis, which is why the neutrophil count is monitored.
Methotrexate inhibits dihydrofolate reductase, so tetrahydrofolate falls and DNA synthesis slows.
Histamine-2 blockers reduce acid but do not require pre-meal dosing the way proton pump inhibitors do, and are less effective for erosive disease.
Aminoglycosides cause kidney injury and hearing loss, and the class can worsen neuromuscular blockade.
A rash after amoxicillin in acute mononucleosis is usually a drug-virus interaction, not a lifelong penicillin allergy.
Metronidazole can cause a disulfiram-like reaction with alcohol, with flushing and vomiting.
Sildenafil inhibits phosphodiesterase-5, so cyclic GMP stays up and vessels dilate. A nitrate plus this drug can drop the blood pressure severely.
Finasteride inhibits 5-alpha reductase, so testosterone is not converted to dihydrotestosterone.
Tamoxifen blocks estrogen receptors in the breast and stimulates uterine tissue, so endometrial proliferation is a risk.
Aminoglycosides can prolong neuromuscular blockade, especially with a blocker or myasthenia.
Bile-acid resins bind other drugs in the gut, so those drugs should not be taken at the same time.
Myasthenia gravis antibodies attack the postsynaptic acetylcholine receptor, so strength fades with use.
An LDH ratio of pleural fluid to serum above 0.6 supports an exudate even when the story is otherwise unclear.
After an ulcer is controlled, aspirin taken for coronary disease is restarted, not stopped for the long term.
A clean-based ulcer does not need endoscopic therapy. High-risk stigmata do.
Eradication is confirmed with a breath or stool-antigen test at least 4 weeks after antibiotics, not with serology, and not while a proton pump inhibitor is still on board.
In the United States, first-line therapy is optimized bismuth quadruple therapy for 14 days, not a 7-day clarithromycin triple as the default.
Tissue transglutaminase IgA is drawn while gluten is still being eaten. Starting a gluten-free diet first can make the test falsely negative.
Dysphagia is an alarm symptom. It gets endoscopy, not another empiric acid-drug course.
Mild acute pancreatitis without infection does not get prophylactic antibiotics.
Mild acute pancreatitis is fed early. A several-day fast is not required once pain and nausea allow eating.
Uncomplicated diverticulitis in an immunocompetent patient who can drink does not automatically need antibiotics.
Adults aged 18 to 79 are screened once for hepatitis C, including people with no reported risk.
Ascitic fluid with at least 250 neutrophils per microliter is treated as spontaneous bacterial peritonitis without waiting for the culture.
Removal of more than 5 liters of ascites is followed by albumin. A small tap does not require that infusion.
Cirrhosis with gastrointestinal bleeding gets short-term antibiotic prophylaxis, not antibiotics only after a fever starts.
A negative tissue-transglutaminase IgA does not clear celiac disease until total IgA is known, because IgA deficiency hides the test.
Typical reflux without alarm symptoms gets an 8-week proton pump inhibitor trial, not immediate endoscopy.
A colitis flare with new diarrhea is tested for C. difficile before immunosuppression is escalated.
A proton pump inhibitor for reflux is taken before a meal, not at bedtime, because the pumps are active with food.
A neutrophil count under 250 in ascites, with no other infection sign, is not spontaneous bacterial peritonitis and does not get the peritonitis antibiotic course.
Knee osteoarthritis is treated first with a topical NSAID, not an opioid and not glucosamine as a required drug.
DMARD-naive rheumatoid arthritis with moderate or high activity starts with methotrexate, not a biologic as the first drug.
Two biologic drugs are not combined in rheumatoid arthritis.
Acute low back pain without a red flag does not get imaging, and it does not start with an opioid.
Nonpurulent cellulitis is treated for streptococci. Empiric MRSA drugs are for purulent infection, not for plain cellulitis.
A drainable abscess is incised. Antibiotics are added when systemic signs are present, and drainage is not skipped.
Women aged 65 and older are screened for osteoporosis with bone-density testing. Age 66 is inside that recommendation.
A postmenopausal woman under 65 without increased fracture risk is not offered routine bone-density screening.
A hip fracture from a fall is enough to start osteoporosis treatment. Densitometry is not a reason to delay the drug.
Axial spondyloarthritis starts with an NSAID trial. A TNF inhibitor is not the first prescription when an NSAID has not been tried.
Newly diagnosed immune thrombocytopenia with platelets under 30,000 is treated with a corticosteroid. A count of 18,000 is already under that line.
Immune thrombocytopenia with platelets of 50,000 and no bleeding is observed. Steroids are not mandatory at that count.
Suspected heparin-induced thrombocytopenia means all heparin stops and a non-heparin anticoagulant starts. Warfarin is not started alone while the platelet count is low.
Stable neutropenic fever starts with one antipseudomonal beta-lactam. Vancomycin is not automatic.
Vancomycin is added to neutropenic fever when the patient is unstable or a catheter infection is suspected, not because the temperature exists.
Platelet transfusion in immune thrombocytopenia is for serious bleeding, not for a low number alone.
Severe albuminuria without diabetes is still a reason to start an ACE inhibitor or an ARB. Moderate albuminuria without diabetes is not the same automatic start.
A rise in creatinine of up to 30 percent after an ACE inhibitor can be accepted. A rise well above 30 percent is reassessed and the drug is reduced or stopped.
A creatinine rise of about 20 percent after an ACE inhibitor is the expected hemodynamic change and is not a reason to stop the drug.
Initial treatment of minimal change disease in adults is high-dose glucocorticoid, not cyclosporine as the first drug.
Asymptomatic bacteriuria in a nonpregnant adult is not treated. Pregnancy is the setting where screening and treatment apply.
Uncomplicated cystitis is treated with nitrofurantoin, trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, or fosfomycin. A fluoroquinolone is not the first drug.
Pyelonephritis is not treated with nitrofurantoin. That drug does not reach reliable kidney levels.
Thrombolysis is not given until blood pressure is below 185/110 mm Hg. A pressure of 200/120 has to come down first.
Aspirin is given after ischemic stroke, but not within 24 hours of thrombolysis.
Convulsive status epilepticus is treated first with a benzodiazepine, not with phenytoin as the opening drug.
Benzodiazepines are not used for posttraumatic stress disorder. Trauma-focused psychotherapy is the preferred treatment.
Major depression is treated with psychotherapy or an antidepressant such as an SSRI. A benzodiazepine is not the antidepressant.
Bipolar depression is not treated with antidepressant monotherapy. A mood stabilizer or an approved bipolar regimen is used.
Schizophrenia is started on one antipsychotic. Two antipsychotics are not begun together.
Naltrexone helps alcohol use disorder only when the patient is not taking an opioid. An opioid use history that is current makes naltrexone the wrong drug.
Alcohol withdrawal is treated with a benzodiazepine. An antipsychotic is not the withdrawal drug.
Buprenorphine for opioid use disorder can start without a completed inpatient detox. Detox alone is not the treatment.
A healthy adult with outpatient pneumonia is treated with amoxicillin or doxycycline, not a fluoroquinolone as the first drug.
Outpatient pneumonia plus chronic heart or lung disease uses combination therapy or a respiratory fluoroquinolone, not amoxicillin alone.
Uncomplicated acute bronchitis in a healthy adult does not get an antibiotic.
A long-acting beta agonist is never used as the only asthma drug. It has to be paired with an inhaled corticosteroid.
Nonvalvular atrial fibrillation with a high stroke score is anticoagulated with a DOAC. Aspirin alone is not the stroke drug.
A mechanical mitral valve is anticoagulated with warfarin. A DOAC is not a substitute.
Moderate or severe mitral stenosis with atrial fibrillation is anticoagulated with warfarin, not a DOAC.
A nitrate and a phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitor together can cause severe hypotension. The combination is contraindicated.
Symptomatic severe aortic stenosis is referred for valve replacement. Medical therapy does not replace the valve.
Hypothyroidism in pregnancy is treated by increasing levothyroxine. Methimazole is not a treatment for a high TSH.
In the first trimester, propylthiouracil is preferred over methimazole for hyperthyroidism because methimazole is more teratogenic then.
If potassium is below 3.3 mEq/L in diabetic ketoacidosis, potassium is replaced before insulin. Insulin would drive the potassium lower.
Migraine with aura makes combined hormonal contraception an unacceptable risk. A progestin-only method does not carry that same estrogen risk.
Long-term metformin is associated with vitamin B12 deficiency. Numbness or anemia is a reason to check B12, not to ignore it because glucose is controlled.
Strongly anticholinergic drugs such as oxybutynin are avoided in older adults because of confusion, constipation, and falls.
When immune thrombocytopenia needs a rapid platelet rise for surgery or serious bleeding, IVIG or a similar rescue is used. Steroids alone are too slow for that emergency.
Platelet transfusion is not given for the low count of heparin-induced thrombocytopenia unless there is serious bleeding.
Iron deficiency anemia in a postmenopausal woman is evaluated with bidirectional endoscopy, not iron tablets alone.
Cancer-associated venous thrombosis is treated with a DOAC or low-molecular-weight heparin, not warfarin as the automatic first drug.
Moderate or severe obstructive sleep apnea is treated with positive airway pressure, not with a sedative as the sleep drug.
Suspected adrenal crisis is treated immediately with intravenous hydrocortisone and saline. A lab result is not required before the first dose.
Asymptomatic bacteriuria in pregnancy is treated. The same culture in a nonpregnant adult is not.
When phosphate is high and calcium is already high, a non-calcium binder such as sevelamer is used. More calcium binder would worsen the calcium.
An acute multiple-sclerosis relapse that limits function is treated with high-dose corticosteroid. A disease-modifying injection is not the acute relapse drug.
Guillain-Barre syndrome is treated with intravenous immunoglobulin or plasma exchange. Corticosteroids do not help.
A copper intrauterine device is the most effective emergency contraception and can be placed within 5 days. It is not reserved for people who have already given birth.
Clozapine requires absolute-neutrophil monitoring. It is not started or continued without that lab plan, and it is not the first antipsychotic.
Antiretroviral therapy starts as soon as HIV is diagnosed. A CD4 count is not a reason to delay the first doses.
Pneumocystis prophylaxis starts when the CD4 count is below 200. Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole is the usual drug.
Pain out of proportion, rapid spread, and systemic toxicity are necrotizing infection until proved otherwise. Antibiotics do not replace immediate surgery.
Tinea capitis is treated with an oral antifungal. Topical cream does not reach the hair shaft.
Confirmed group A streptococcal pharyngitis is treated with penicillin or amoxicillin. A fluoroquinolone is not the drug.
Chronic low back pain is treated first with exercise and other non-drug care. An opioid is not the first prescription.
NSAIDs are avoided in advanced chronic kidney disease because the class reduces filtration. Pain is treated with a different class.
The first hour of a new neutropenic fever is an antibacterial emergency, not an automatic antifungal start.
Acute venous thrombosis in pregnancy is treated with low-molecular-weight heparin. Warfarin and DOACs are not the pregnancy drugs.
Cluster headache attacks are treated with 100 percent oxygen or a triptan. An opioid is not the acute treatment.
Serotonin syndrome is treated by stopping the serotonergic drugs. Adding another serotonergic drug makes it worse.
Methotrexate is stopped before a planned pregnancy. It is teratogenic and is not continued in order to keep joints quiet.
Neuroleptic malignant syndrome is treated by stopping the antipsychotic. Rigidity and a very high temperature after a dose increase are not a reason to give more.
A toxic acetaminophen level or a history of a large ingestion is treated with acetylcysteine. Waiting for liver-enzyme failure misses the window.
Benzodiazepines are avoided for insomnia in older adults because of falls and confusion.
Community-acquired pneumonia that is improving is treated for about 5 days, not a reflexive 14-day course.
If serology suggests celiac disease, the duodenal biopsy is done while gluten is still being eaten.
Unintentional weight loss with reflux is an alarm symptom and is investigated, not treated with a longer empiric acid-drug course.
Chronic metabolic acidosis in CKD, with bicarbonate well below normal, is treated with oral alkali. It is not ignored until bicarbonate is under 8.
Delirium in an older adult is a reason to find the cause, not to start a benzodiazepine as the calming drug.
The edge of cellulitis is marked and rechecked. Spreading redness on antibiotics is a reason to reassess, not to wait out a fixed 10-day prescription.
ACE inhibitors are stopped before pregnancy because the class is teratogenic. A beta blocker or another allowed drug replaces the blood-pressure treatment.
